title: Operational dependability field notes and interlock plan
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working field-notes style project plan for the Operational Dependability initiative: to align SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, Product (Console), and Solutions teams on SLO cadence, capacity fallback policies, and interlock points for Q1–Q2 2027. It intentionally mixes tactical sprint tasks, meeting rhythms, and unresolved questions so stakeholders can iterate in-place.

High-level objectives (what success looks like):
- Clear, testable service SLO matrix that maps to product-facing promises and internal error budgets.
- A two-tier fallback policy (regional + model-variant) implemented in smart-routing for top-10 customer flows.
- Capacity simulation and chaos test plan run twice before GA-targeted launches.
- Communication and escalation flows defined and rehearsed (runbook triggers, on-call playbooks, executive notification).
- Measurable improvement in 99th percentile p95/p99 token latency and end-to-end availability for hosted inference routes.

Primary owners and stakeholders:
- Initiative lead: Aisha Patel (platform-engineering) — program coordinator and primary contact
- SRE partner: Marco Ruiz (site-reliability-engineering) — SLO definitions, oncall/runbook
- Serving runtime lead: Dana Kim (serving-runtime) — capacity & failover kernel changes
- Product/Console: Jamal Thompson (product-console) — reporting, user-facing SLO mapping
- Solutions/CS: Sophie Laurent (solutions-engineering-and-professional-services) — customer impact scenarios and pilot coordination
- Security & Compliance: (advisory) Priya Nair — review for Private deployments fallback docs

Stakeholder RACI (short):
- Define SLOs: R=Aisha, A=Marco, C=Jamal,D=Dana
- Implement fallback routing: R=Dana, A=Aisha, C=Marco
- Capacity simulation: R=Marco, A=Dana, C=Platform
- Console-level SLA mapping: R=Jamal, A=Aisha

Proposed SLO matrix (draft values — review with product stakeholders):
- Hosted API (text generation): availability 99.95% monthly, latency p95 < 600ms, p99 < 1.2s
- Chat streaming: availability 99.9% monthly, median stream latency < 200ms, p95 < 500ms
- Embeddings endpoint: availability 99.99% monthly, batch throughput >= X req/s per shard (simulation to determine X)
- Private deployments: availability 99.9% monthly (contract-dep), p95 latency target matched to customer's region

Notes on measurement:
- Use tracing + token-level telemetry from Console agent and Serving Runtime traces to compute per-route SLOs.
- Ground truth source: Prometheus + Honeycomb traces with SLO rollups in the Console dashboard — ensure single definition of truth (avoid duplicate counters).
- Error budget policy: 14-day rolling windows for canary decisions, monthly windows for escalations.

Fallback & routing policy (sketch):
1) Primary region route — if latency or error rate crosses warn threshold (70% of SLO) for >3m, start local KV-cache-only mode (short-circuit non-essential transforms)
2) If condition persists >10m or error budget burn >X%: route to tiered model-variant (quantized, smaller-context) in same region
3) If region capacity exhausted or region outage: route to adjacent region with capacity but degrade to model-variant + lower decoding tokens/shorter max-length policy
4) Customer-specific: for Dedicated/Private customers with pinned variants, fallback to pre-agreed alternate endpoints or throttle with explicit customer notification

Tasks & Milestones (12-week initial window):
- Week 0–2: Finalize SLO draft and acceptance criteria (owners: Aisha + Marco). Run stakeholder review with Product and CS.
- Week 2–4: Instrument Console and runtime to expose SLO signals (traces, error categories). Quick PRs: runtime telemetry gating + console metrics mapping.
- Week 4–6: Implement first-pass routing policy in canary mode for one non-critical route (embeddings) — observe and collect metrics.
- Week 6–8: Run capacity simulation and chaos tests (lossy network / node drain) against canary route. Record burn rates.
- Week 8–10: Iterate routing policy (policy tweaks, faster short-circuit paths) and expand to two additional routes (chat-streaming and hosted generation).
- Week 10–12: Stakeholder readiness review, runbook rehearsals, and small customer pilot for fallback behavior. Decide GA gating for Q2 launches.

Sprint checklist (to copy into tickets):
- Owner assigned and CCR updated
- Acceptance criteria: measurable SLO metrics + test scenarios
- Monitoring: dashboards created + alert thresholds documented
- Runbook: playbooks for warn/critical events, escalation matrix mapped to oncall
- Docs: Confluence page + linked PRs and release notes

Communication cadence and rituals:
- Weekly interlock (30m) on Mon 10:30 PT — quick updates, blockers, action owners (invite: Aisha, Marco, Dana, Jamal, Sophie)
- Biweekly deeper sync (60m) for policy review and simulation results
- Slack channel: #ops-dependability (use for async updates, link to runbooks and incidents)
- Pre-flight checklist meeting 48h before any canary expand or chaos run — require signoff from SRE, Runtime, Platform

Runbook & incident triggers (draft):
- Warn trigger: route p95 > 70% SLO or error-rate increase 3x baseline sustained 3 minutes — notify #ops-dependability and paging to SRE rotation
- Escalation trigger: p95 > 90% SLO or error budget burn > 50% in 14-day window — runbook owner runs traffic shift + exec notice if GA route impacted
- Degradation trigger: regional outage detected by cloud provider or region heartbeat loss — execute regional failover checklist and track customer impact matrix

Capacity planning & simulation notes:
- Work with Infra to produce a small simulation harness that injects synthetic requests matching top-20 customer prompt length distribution. We need median, p95, p99 latency curves vs concurrency.
- Baseline goals: run 2x expected traffic in simulation and validate fallbacks keep p95 within acceptable line for 95% of customers.
- Define cost/latency tradeoff points where routing policy prefers model-variant vs cross-region failover.

Open questions / risk register (short):
- Q: How do we measure semantic correctness/regression when using quantized model-variants as fallbacks? (risk: customer-visible hallucinations) — Action: research small test suite and human-eval checklist for critical flows (owner: Solutions)
- Q: Can we safely short-circuit non-essential transforms for some customers without breaking their downstream pipelines? — Action: Product to flag customers that opt-out by config
- Risk: Duplicate SLO definitions living in Console and in separate dashboards — mitigate by creating single SLO source-of-truth PR (owner: Jamal)
- Risk: On-call noise from early canaries — mitigate by tuned alert thresholds and quiet-window for canary test runs

Acceptance and GA gating checklist (minimum):
- SLO computation validated end-to-end and dashboarded
- Fallback policies implemented in canary, tested under chaos, and show acceptable degradation behavior
- Runbooks authored and practiced (1 tabletop + 1 live drill)
- Customer pilot (2–3 customers) run, feedback logged, no critical regressions in correctness tests

Housekeeping & docs to produce (this doc tracks initial deliverables):
- Confluence: Operational Dependability program page (canonical SLO matrix, tickets, meeting notes)
- Playbooks: runbook WARN/ESCALATION/DEGRADATION checklists per route
- GH: runtime PRs and policy config merge requests with changelog entries
- Jira: task board under ENG-RELDEP (placeholder project key) with tagged epics for SLOs, routing, simulations, runbooks

Quick notes to self (informal):
- Keep the first canary on a low-risk route (embeddings) — we can measure backlog and retries cheaply
- Make sure Solutions team builds a tiny human-eval checklist for the top 5 prompt types for fallback correctness — cheap manual checks beat blind rollouts
- Align with Security early on Private fallback docs (customers care about data flows between regions)

Immediate next actions (today / next 3 days):
- Aisha: schedule weekly interlock and create Confluence page stub + attach this doc
- Marco: draft SLO rollup Prometheus query examples and share in the interlock meeting
- Dana: scope minimal runtime telemetry PR and estimate effort (story points)
- Jamal: draft mapping table from Console routes to product-facing promises (SLA language)

Appendix: useful links & refs
- Reliability playbook (internal): https://confluence.redwood/team/reliability-playbook
- Recommended chaos tests repo: github.com/redwood-inference/ops-chaos (see pr/42)

End of notes — treat as living doc. Update last_modified when major changes occur and date-stamp the section header with the change summary.

Unresolved edits log:

- 2027-01-07: inserted acceptance gating checklist and added human-eval item (Sophie)
- 2027-01-10: tuned SLO draft numbers after product review (Jamal)
